steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK film industry operates on a significantly smaller scale than Hollywood, with lower budgets, fewer productions and greater dependence on public funding and international co-productions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The British Film Institute (BFI) is the lead organisation for film in the UK, distributing National Lottery funding to support film production, distribution, education and cultural exhibition.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: National Lottery funding has been crucial to British film production, financing films that commercial investors would consider too risky, culturally specific or unlikely to generate mass returns.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: UK film production frequently relies on co-production deals with US studios or international partners, providing access to larger budgets but potentially compromising creative control and British cultural identity.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use specific examples of UK films and their funding sources to demonstrate understanding of the industry structure. Explain how the UK film industry's structure — small scale, public funding, co-production — directly affects the films audiences see. Compare the UK industry with Hollywood to highlight what is distinctive about British film production and distribution. Understand the role of the BFI and public funding as defining features that distinguish the UK industry from the US model. Consider how industry constraints create both limitations and opportunities for British filmmakers.
